t: Maximum Total Beauty of the Gardens
o: Sort gardens ascending. Any optimal plan fills some suffix of the sorted array up to target (making them 'full') and uses leftover flowers to raise the minimum of the remaining prefix. In example 2, filling 3 gardens costs 5 flowers, leaving 5 flowers to raise the minimum of [4] to... actually the min of the incomplete set {4} becomes 4 with 0 spent, beauty 3*2+4*6=30. Because newFlowers can be 1e10 and n is 1e5, we need prefix sums and a per-candidate-count binary search rather than simulation. Key observation: it is never beneficial to partially fill a garden above target-1 without completing it, and the gardens we complete should be the tallest ones.
k: In an optimal solution, completed gardens form a suffix of the sorted array.
Given a fixed set of completed gardens, maximizing the minimum of the rest is a monotone binary search on the target minimum value using prefix sums.
Try every possible number of completed gardens (0..n) and take the best; costs fit in 64-bit integers.

a.n: Sort + Prefix Sums + Binary Search per Candidate
a.i: Sort ascending and build prefix sums. Iterate j = number of completed gardens (the j tallest). The cost to lift them to target is computed incrementally. With remaining budget rem, binary search the largest value v < target such that raising all m = n-j remaining gardens to v costs v*m - pre[m] <= rem. Beauty = j*full + v*partial; also handle the all-complete case.
s: Sort flowers ascending; build prefix sums pre[].
Start with j = count of gardens already >= target (they are free completions).
For each j: with rem = newFlowers - costSoFar, binary search max v in [0, target-1] with v*m - pre[m] <= rem; update answer.
Try to extend j by paying target - flowers[next] if budget allows; stop when unaffordable or all complete.
a.t: O(n log n + n log target) — sorting plus one binary search per candidate completion count.

w: Common pitfalls: forgetting the case where all gardens become complete (partial term must be dropped), 32-bit overflow (newFlowers up to 1e10, products up to ~1e15), and assuming already-complete gardens shouldn't be counted. A two-pointer version removes the inner binary search for O(n log n) overall; mention it if asked to optimize further.
